source.title: Thin Orchestrator: The AI agent architecture that made our internal tools more reliable

read_evidence.scope: Complete engineering article: earlier broad-agent failure modes, approximately 1,300-line orchestrator, deterministic routing, more than 20 workflows, 14 specialists, context isolation, typed handoffs, bounded tools, internal speed and revision results, and publisher-reported limitations.

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Approximate publisher reading time; no individual reading session measured.

complete_compiler_story.summary: Meta describes replacing a broad agent with a roughly 1,300-line orchestrator that routes requests to 14 context-isolated specialists across more than 20 workflows. The design uses deterministic routing, typed handoffs and narrow tool access. Meta reports much faster delivery and fewer edits, but the results come from its internal engineering environment.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Separate coordination from domain work when one agent’s context becomes noisy. Define explicit routes, minimal handoff fields and bounded tools, then compare completion quality and human revision rates before assuming that additional specialists improve reliability.

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Approximate publisher reading time; no individual reading session measured.

complete_compiler_story.summary: Plaud’s Skills feature saves reusable instruction sets that can be created from templates, conversations, files, forms or artifacts, then invoked automatically in Work mode. Users review a draft before saving, and the platform limits each workspace to 100 skills. Usage consumes Plaud Credits, so repeatability still needs cost and quality checks.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Create one meeting-decision skill that extracts decisions, owners, deadlines and open questions with transcript evidence. Test it on three varied recordings, compare every claim with the source, and require human approval before saving the skill or sharing its brief.
complete_compiler_story.related_coverage: Other October 21 stories cover inference operations, orchestration boundaries, workplace context, public-sector review, biopharma coordination and reusable meeting skills.
complete_compiler_story.image_alt_intent: Three meeting transcripts flow through a reusable decision-brief skill into reviewed cards for decisions, owners, deadlines, open questions and traceable evidence.
complete_compiler_story.agent_skills_evidence: Create a reusable `meeting-decision-brief` Skill for recorded discussions. Accept one recording or transcript plus the meeting purpose and participant list. Extract decisions, named owners, stated deadlines and unresolved questions; attach a verbatim evidence pointer to every item; flag uncertainty rather than guessing; and return a structured brief. Review the generated draft before saving. Test three fixtures covering a clear decision, conflicting owner statements and an unstated deadline. The Skill never sends messages, changes calendars or assigns work. A human must compare each item with the source and approve both the saved procedure and every distributed brief.

audience_fit.intended_user: Consultants, project managers and meeting facilitators who repeatedly convert recorded discussions into decision-ready briefs.
audience_fit.practical_action: Create a meeting-decision Skill from a reviewed template that extracts decisions, owners, deadlines and unresolved questions.
audience_fit.review_action: Compare every extracted decision, owner and deadline with the recording or transcript before saving or sharing the brief.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A consistent decision brief with traceable evidence, explicit open questions and clearly assigned human follow-up.
